A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SYMPOL study. All 33 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original control and MiniGrid experiments, PPO/A2C comparisons, ablations and a DistShift misgeneralization case study.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the same GradTree actor, neural critic, straight-through optimization, selective weight decay, continuous-action formulation and dynamic rollout/batch procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five control environments and MiniGrid tasks, including both LavaGap sizes and the randomized DistShift scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain MLP, SDT, D-SDT and SA-DT at depths 5 and 8. VIPER at depths 5 and 8 remains evaluated in Appendix A.3, Tables 8–9.

E3.justification: The one-million-timestep training budget, 60-trial hyperparameter optimization, PPO/A2C settings and MiniGrid observation setup are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same hyperparameter grids and selected settings.

E4.justification: The four component ablations, tree-size and interpretability analyses, runtime/training-curve analyses and DistShift misgeneralization case study are retained without changes, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random trainings with five evaluation episodes each. Cohen’s D, significance-based table highlighting and graphical uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. For example, SYMPOL retains rewards of 500 on CartPole and -57 on LunarLander in Table 2, and 0.953 on LavaGap-7 in Table 3; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The MDP/PPO definitions and SYMPOL formulations in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. Equation placement and spacing changes introduce no mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about direct optimization, avoiding information loss, interpretability and performance. The added abstract sentence supplies code-access information.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning categorical inductive bias, training stability, interpretability and goal misgeneralization remain unchanged. Existing applicability boundaries and future-work discussion are also retained.

D1.justification: v3 describes code in supplementary material and promises public release upon acceptance. v5 provides an explicit s-marton/sympol repository address in the abstract and Section 5.1 footnote; implementation, hardware and hyperparameter details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The Xu et al. and Kamienny et al. entries match the same titled 2022 work, Symbolic-model-based reinforcement learning, with revised author/venue metadata. Existing citations and passages are regrouped in Section 2, while literature coverage and substantive positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2 moves the reward-function and ensemble discussion earlier, tightens the VIPER description and fixes the reference to the 'third line' under item (2). Other edits are limited wording, bibliographic and code-access updates.

P2.justification: The longer abstract shifts Figure 1 and the introduction downward; equation spacing, the new code footnote and reference-page spacing also change. Figure and table contents, structures and captions are retained, and the appendices render identically.

improvement.justification: v5 improves code-access instructions by replacing a future-release promise with an explicit repository address, and makes small readability fixes in Section 2. These are limited practical improvements; the scientific content and appendix evidence are unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository’s contents or usability.
